The variable instance has Multi-value enabled. Which PromQL filter works when several values are selected?
up{instance=~"$instance"}
up{instance="$instance"}
up{instance=="$instance"}
up{instance~"$instance"}
Grafana expands multiple values into a regex like (a|b), so the regex matcher =~ is needed.
Which built-in variable does Grafana recommend as the range in rate() queries against Prometheus?
$__rate_interval
$__interval_ms
$__range
$__from
$__rate_interval is at least four scrape intervals and adapts to the zoom level, avoiding empty or misleading rate() results.
What does the Repeat option on a panel do?
Creates one copy of the panel for each selected variable value
Re-runs the panel's query every few seconds
Duplicates the panel into another dashboard
Repeats the same series twice for comparison
Repeating by a variable, for example one panel per server, keeps dashboards dynamic without manual copies.
Which visualization fits CPU usage of several servers over the last 24 hours?
Time series
Pie chart
Stat
Text
Time series panels draw values over time as lines or bars. Stat shows a single current value.
Which visualization shows one big current value, such as active users, with an optional sparkline?
Stat
Table
Heatmap
Node graph
Stat panels highlight a single value with color by threshold and an optional background graph.
In Grafana Alerting, what is a contact point?
A set of destinations, such as email or Slack, that receive notifications
The query and condition that decide when an alert fires
The person who acknowledged an alert first
The data source the alert rule reads from
Contact points define where notifications go. The query and condition belong to the alert rule itself.
In Grafana Alerting, what decides which contact point receives a firing alert, based on its labels?
Notification policies
Silences
Mute timings
Data source permissions
Notification policies form a routing tree that matches alert labels to contact points and sets grouping and timing.
A Grafana alert rule has a pending period of 5 minutes. What does that mean?
The condition must stay true for 5 minutes before the alert fires
Notifications are sent again every 5 minutes
The rule is evaluated once every 5 minutes
The alert resolves itself after 5 minutes
During the pending period the alert is Pending. Only if the condition still holds afterwards does it switch to Firing.
opentelemetry: Which are OpenTelemetry's three core, stable telemetry signals?
Traces, metrics and logs
Traces, alerts and dashboards
Metrics, events and SLAs
Logs, incidents and uptime
Traces, metrics and logs are the main signals. Profiling is a newer, separate signal.
What is a span in OpenTelemetry?
One timed operation in a trace, with attributes and a parent
A full request across all services from start to end
A metric that counts errors over a time window
A log file written by a single service
A trace is a tree of spans. Each span records start and end time, attributes, events, status and its parent span id.
What do all spans belonging to one trace share?
The same trace ID
The same span ID
The same service name
The same start time
Every span has its own span ID, but all spans of a trace carry the same trace ID, which ties them together across services.
A service sets OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=parentbased_traceidratio and OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG=0.1. What happens?
About 10% of new traces sampled; children follow the parent
Exactly every tenth span is exported, ignoring parents
10% of spans are dropped and the rest are exported
Each span is kept for 0.1 seconds before export
The root sampler keeps a ratio of traces based on trace ID, and parent-based sampling keeps decisions consistent across a trace.
By default, which HTTP header do OpenTelemetry SDKs use to propagate trace context?
traceparent (W3C Trace Context)
X-B3-TraceId (Zipkin B3)
uber-trace-id (Jaeger)
X-Request-ID
The default propagators are W3C Trace Context and W3C Baggage. B3 and Jaeger formats are available as extra propagators.
Service A makes an outgoing HTTP call to service B. Which span kind should A's span for the call have?
CLIENT
SERVER
PRODUCER
INTERNAL
The caller records a CLIENT span and the receiving service records a SERVER span. PRODUCER is for asynchronous messaging.
An operation failed and you want its span marked as failed. What do you set?
The span status to Error
The span kind to INTERNAL
A new trace ID for the span
The span name to error
Span status can be Unset, Ok or Error. Setting Error, often with a recorded exception event, marks the failure for backends.
What is Baggage in OpenTelemetry?
Key-value pairs propagated across services along with the context
Spans held in memory before the exporter sends them
Attributes attached only to the root span
Logs that are dropped when the buffer is full
Baggage carries values such as a tenant id across process boundaries. It is not added to spans automatically.
Which metric instrument fits the number of requests currently in progress, which goes up and down?
UpDownCounter
Counter
Histogram
ObservableCounter
UpDownCounter allows increments and decrements. Counter and ObservableCounter are monotonic, and Histogram records distributions.
Which metric instrument should record request durations so that you can compute percentiles later?
Histogram
Counter
UpDownCounter
Gauge
Histograms aggregate measurements into buckets, from which backends estimate percentiles such as p95.
How does OpenTelemetry correlate a log record with a trace?
The log record carries the active span's trace and span IDs
The log message text includes the service name
Logs are written into span names when they occur
The Collector matches logs to traces by timestamp
When logs are emitted within an active span, SDKs and log bridges attach its trace and span IDs, so backends can jump between them.
Which three component types make up a pipeline in the OpenTelemetry Collector?
Receivers, processors and exporters
Agents, brokers and dashboards
Inputs, filters and alerts
Scrapers, indexers and viewers
Receivers ingest data, processors transform it and exporters send it to backends. Connectors can link pipelines.
What is the main purpose of the batch processor in the Collector?
Grouping telemetry before export to cut request count
Sampling traces so that only errors are kept
Converting metrics into log records
Retrying data that failed to export
Batching cuts the number of outgoing connections and improves throughput.
What does the memory_limiter processor do in the Collector?
Refuses data when memory is too high, to avoid crashes
Compresses data in memory before sending it
Limits how many spans each trace can contain
Moves old data from memory to the disk
memory_limiter applies backpressure when limits are reached. It is recommended as the first processor in each pipeline.
What does running the Collector in agent mode mean?
It runs next to the app, for example as a sidecar or DaemonSet
It runs inside the application process as a library
It runs as the central gateway for the whole company
It runs only during tests, not in production
Agents run on the same host or pod as the app. Gateways are separate central Collector deployments that agents can forward to.
A receiver is configured in the receivers section but not listed in any pipeline under service. What happens?
It is not enabled
It is added to every pipeline
The Collector fails to start
It runs but drops all data
Components only become active when referenced in service.pipelines. Defining them alone does nothing.
How do you add zero-code (automatic) instrumentation to a Java application?
Attach the OpenTelemetry Java agent with the -javaagent flag
Add an @OpenTelemetry annotation to each class
Recompile the JVM with tracing support
Run the Collector with the java receiver
The Java agent instruments popular libraries at runtime through bytecode manipulation, without code changes.
What does an instrumentation library, such as the one for Express or Flask, provide?
Telemetry for that library's operations, without writing spans by hand
A backend that stores and displays traces
A replacement for the framework with tracing built in
Load balancing between instrumented services
Instrumentation libraries hook into frameworks and clients to create spans and metrics for requests, queries and calls.
Which are the default OTLP ports?
4317 for gRPC and 4318 for HTTP
4318 for gRPC and 4317 for HTTP
9090 for gRPC and 9091 for HTTP
14250 for gRPC and 14268 for HTTP
OTLP uses 4317 for gRPC and 4318 for HTTP/protobuf. 14250 and 14268 are legacy Jaeger ports.
Which environment variable sets the OTLP endpoint used by SDK exporters?
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
OTEL_COLLECTOR_URL
OTLP_EXPORTER_HOST
OTEL_ENDPOINT_URL
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT applies to all signals; per-signal variants such as OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT override it.
